text: My great-aunt Rosalía raised chickens behind her house in Oaxaca. Every Sunday she made mole negro and would not let anyone help stir it. She hummed while she cooked but I never learned the song.
Grandpa Teodoro fixed radios for the whole street. He always said 'Everything broken just needs patience.' He drank his coffee with too much sugar.
My friend Dani loved skateboarding and terrible puns. We used to split a bag of Takis after school. I don't remember what music she liked.
Abuela Carmen sang 'Cielito Lindo' every time it rained. She kept a tin of buttons from every coat she ever owned.
Uncle Beto was a bus driver for thirty years. He knew every passenger's name. He liked tamales, I think the green ones, but maybe that was my mom.
My neighbor Mrs. Okafor grew tomatoes on her balcony and gave them to everyone. She called me 'little professor' because I always carried books.
Tío Ernesto played dominoes at the plaza every evening and never lost gracefully. He wore the same brown hat for years.
My grandmother Lucía made pan de muerto with orange zest. She told the story of crossing the river with my mother on her back.
Our dog Pepita waited by the door every day at five. She stole socks.
Grandpa Hiro taught me chess on a board with one missing knight, replaced by a bottle cap. He liked jazz, but I can't remember which records.
Mamá Inés wrote letters to everyone in green ink. She loved marigolds and planted them every October.
My cousin Javi fixed bikes and made the best chilaquiles. He laughed so loud the neighbors complained.
